title: Zoox can now charge for rides in its steering-wheel-free robotaxis
excerpt: Zoox has won approval to charge for robotaxi rides in the US. Under an exemption from the NHTSA, Zoox can deploy up to 5,000 vehicles over the next two years.
content_html:
Emma Roth

is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Zoox just got permission to charge for robotaxi rides in its boxy, steering-wheel-less vehicles. On Thursday, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration announced it has granted the Amazon-owned Zoox a temporary exemption, allowing it to deploy up to 2,500 vehicles annually over the next two years, as reported earlier by Reuters.

The NHTSA’s decision exempts Zoox from rules requiring vehicles to have traditional controls, like a steering wheel, pedals, windshield defrosting, and mirrors. Zoox’s vehicles are built with passengers in mind, rather than drivers, featuring an interior with two bench seats and sliding doors. Until now, Zoox had been providing free rides to people in San Francisco and Las Vegas under a “demonstration exemption.” It had been waiting on approval for paid rides from the NHTSA, which has taken steps in recent months to streamline approvals for autonomous vehicles.

The move will allow Zoox to compete against Google’s Waymo and Elon Musk’s Tesla robotaxi service, both of which have been expanding their services across the US. Zoox will begin charging fares in Las Vegas next month, according to a press release. The company plans to bring its service to Miami and Austin as well.

In its decision, the NHTSA says it determined that Zoox robotaxis “have an equivalent or greater level of motor vehicle safety” compared to vehicles compliant with federal vehicle safety standards. Under the exemption, Zoox will be subject to “an enhanced oversight condition” that “may update and expand” as the company’s self-driving technology evolves. Zoox issued a software recall for its vehicles earlier this month over concerns that they may not detect smoke.

content_html_zh:
艾玛·罗斯

是一位新闻撰稿人，报道流媒体战争、消费技术、加密货币、社交媒体等。 此前，她是 MUO 的作家和编辑。

Zoox 刚刚获得许可，可以对其四四方方、无方向盘的自动驾驶出租车收费。 据路透社早些时候报道，周四，美国国家公路交通安全管理局宣布已授予亚马逊旗下的 Zoox 临时豁免权，允许其在未来两年内每年部署最多 2,500 辆车辆。

NHTSA 的决定使 Zoox 免受要求车辆配备传统控制装置（如方向盘、踏板、挡风玻璃除霜和后视镜）的规定的约束。 Zoox 的车辆在设计时考虑的是乘客，而不是驾驶员，其内部配有两个长椅和滑动门。 到目前为止，Zoox 一直在“示范豁免”下为旧金山和拉斯维加斯的人们提供免费乘车服务。 它一直在等待国家公路交通安全管理局批准付费乘车服务，近几个月来，国家公路交通安全管理局已采取措施简化自动驾驶汽车的审批。

此举将使 Zoox 能够与谷歌的 Waymo 和埃隆·马斯克的特斯拉机器人出租车服务竞争，这两家公司一直在将服务扩展到美国各地。 据一份新闻稿称，Zoox 将于下个月开始在拉斯维加斯收费。 该公司还计划将其服务带到迈阿密和奥斯汀。

NHTSA 在其决定中表示，与符合联邦车辆安全标准的车辆相比，它确定 Zoox 机器人出租车“具有同等或更高水平的机动车辆安全性”。 根据豁免规定，Zoox 将受到“增强的监督条件”的约束，随着该公司自动驾驶技术的发展，该条件“可能会更新和扩展”。 Zoox 本月早些时候对其车辆进行了软件召回，原因是担心它们可能无法检测到烟雾。
